incident.body:
# Burst saturation incident review

Fictional engineering fixture. Incident IR-08, release 2.4.

A burst of 4,000 events per second from one tenant saturated the dispatch queue.
Queue depth reached 18,000 events within 90 seconds.
The gateway continued accepting events while dispatch p95 latency rose to 12 seconds.
The tenant concurrency budget was enforced, but the shared retry scheduler became congested.
The overload guard incorrectly used gateway latency instead of queue age.

## Corrective decision
Pause the full rollout until the overload guard uses oldest-event age.
Keep the 10 percent canary active with the burst traffic generator disabled.
Repeat the burst test after the scheduler fairness patch and overload guard are deployed.
Passing the steady-state load test does not satisfy the burst acceptance gate.

incident.label: S1

Release 2.4 introduces per-tenant dispatch concurrency budgets and receipt tracing.
The gateway rejects payloads larger than 256 KiB before they reach the queue.
Worker retry delays now honor bounded Retry-After hints.
The delivery ledger distinguishes confirmed receipts from ambiguous outcomes.

cases.question: What was the steady state gateway p95 latency?

hits.body:
# Steady-state load test

Fictional engineering fixture. Run LT-24, release 2.4.

The steady-state test delivered 600 events per second for 30 minutes.
The workload used 16 tenants, uniform 8 KiB payloads, and a 20 ms worker response delay.
Observed gateway p95 latency was 43 ms; dispatch p95 latency was 118 ms.
The acceptance limits were 75 ms for gateway p95 and 200 ms for dispatch p95.
The steady-state acceptance gates passed.

## Limits
This run did not simulate sudden bursts, tenant imbalance, or downstream outages.
It does not establish the maximum sustainable capacity of the service.
Queue depth stayed below 400 events throughout this fixture run.
The source contains invented measurements for demonstrating evidence inspection.

# Rollout acceptance checklist

Fictional engineering fixture. Change CR-24.

The release begins at a 10 percent canary, then advances to 25, 50, and 100 percent.
Each stage requires 20 minutes without a rollback trigger.
Pause rollout when oldest-event age exceeds 30 seconds for three consecutive minutes.
Roll back when permanent rejection rate exceeds 0.5 percent over a five minute window.
The operator records both the trigger and the source dashboard before changing traffic.

## Required evidence
Steady-state load, burst saturation, and worker-outage tests must pass independently.
A green gateway health probe alone cannot establish dispatch readiness.
The release approver needs a signed checklist and links to all three test reports.
The burst saturation gate is currently open, according to incident IR-08.

cases.question: How many delivery attempts are allowed?

hits.body:
# Retry and dead-letter policy

Fictional engineering fixture. Policy RP-03.

Retry transient worker failures with exponential backoff starting at two seconds.
Apply jitter within 20 percent of the scheduled delay to avoid synchronized retries.
Allow five delivery attempts; the fifth failure moves the event to the dead-letter ledger.
HTTP 429 and 503 responses are retryable. HTTP 400 is a permanent rejection.
Use a server Retry-After hint when present, bounded by the 15 minute retry ceiling.

## Receipts
The worker must echo the original event key in its delivery receipt.
A missing receipt is recorded as an ambiguous delivery outcome.
Operators investigate ambiguous outcomes before manually redelivering an event.
The policy makes no promise that arbitrary downstream side effects happen exactly once.

hits.label: S1

hits.body:
# Aster Relay architecture

Fictional engineering fixture. Service: Aster Relay 2.4.

Relay accepts events, writes them to a durable queue, and dispatches them to subscribed workers.
The gateway acknowledges an event only after the queue transaction commits.
Each tenant has an independent concurrency budget of 32 active dispatches.
Worker receipts include an event key, attempt number, and delivery timestamp.
The retry scheduler owns delayed delivery; the gateway does not sleep on worker failures.
Payloads are limited to 256 KiB. Larger payloads are rejected before enqueueing.

## Storage boundary
The event log is append-only. A delivery receipt is separate from the original event.
The queue keeps undelivered events for seven days, then moves them to an expired-events ledger.
The ledger is an operational record, not an automatic replay queue.

cases.question: Where are worker access tokens stored?

hits.body:
# Token isolation and retention review

Fictional engineering fixture. Review SR-11.

Worker access tokens remain in the dispatch service's secret store.
The browser receives a job status identifier, never a worker token.
The event payload retention period is seven days.
Delivery metadata is retained for 30 days for operational diagnosis.
Tenant names are omitted from aggregate latency reports.

## Review notes
Redact Authorization headers from error logs and trace exports.
The review checked the gateway-to-worker credential boundary using dummy tokens.
It did not evaluate a live identity provider or establish regulatory compliance.
Rotate a worker token without interrupting another tenant's delivery budget.
hits.title: security-review.md
hits.label: S1

hits.body:
# Worker outage recovery test

Fictional engineering fixture. Run WO-06.

The worker-outage test removed all workers for 120 seconds while the gateway accepted events.
The queue retained the accepted events and resumed dispatch after workers returned.
The oldest-event age returned below 30 seconds within four minutes of recovery.
No accepted event was absent from the queue's final accounting.
This test used a single retry scheduler and uniform tenant traffic.

## Result
The worker-outage acceptance gate passed for this fixture configuration.
Ambiguous delivery outcomes were counted separately from confirmed worker receipts.
The test did not exercise concurrent scheduler recovery or cross-region failover.
Recovery behavior should not be generalized beyond the stated scenario.
